title: Russian Overnight Strikes Kill 27 Across Ukraine; Russia Formally Excluded from Venice Biennale
detail: The confirmed death toll from Russia's mass overnight strikes across multiple Ukrainian cities and regions rose to 27 by May 6, making it one of the deadliest single-night bombardments of 2026. Rescue operations continued across Zaporizhzhia, Kramatorsk, Dnipro, and the Poltava-Kharkiv gas infrastructure zones. In a separate development reflecting Russia's deepening international isolation, Russia was formally excluded from the Venice Biennale international art exhibition — one of the world's most prestigious cultural events — by organizers citing the ongoing war against Ukraine. The twin developments — mass civilian casualties and cultural exclusion — underscore the continuing humanitarian toll and growing isolation of Moscow as Russia's Victory Day parade approaches on May 9.

media.caption: Russian overnight strikes kill 27 across Ukraine; ceasefire collapse underway — May 6, 2026

title: Russia Violates Ukraine's Declared Ceasefire 1,820 Times in 10 Hours; Zelensky Warns of Symmetric Response
detail: Within the first 10 hours of Ukraine's declared ceasefire (which began midnight May 5–6), President Zelensky reported 1,820 Russian ceasefire violations — including nearly 30 assault operations and more than 20 airstrikes using over 70 guided glide bombs. Russia launched 108 combat drones and 3 missiles overnight between May 5 and 6, striking major cities including Kharkiv. The overnight attacks killed at least 22 people and wounded 82 others. Russia's declared Victory Day ceasefire (May 8–9) came with a simultaneous threat: if Ukraine disrupted the Moscow parade, Russia would launch a 'massive missile strike' on central Kyiv. Zelensky addressed the nation: 'Russia has responded to our proposal for a ceasefire only with new strikes and new attacks... Ukraine will respond in kind.' He stated Ukraine would 'determine our entirely justified responses depending on the situation tonight and tomorrow.' Senior Ukrainian officials also said they saw 'no point' in following Russia's parade-linked ceasefire.

media.caption: Zelensky warns Ukraine will respond in kind after Russia violates declared ceasefire 1,820 times in 10 hours — May 6, 2026
